correctness.rationale: For an original leaf u adjacent through midpoint w to v, name four arcs a:u->w,b:w->u,c:w->v,d:v->w. Every face containing c can add a; remove dominated vertex c by elementary collapse. In the remaining complex every face containing d can add b; delete d. The residual a,b form an S0 join with the once-subdivided bidirected forest after deleting uv. Induction applies for arbitrary branching, components and isolated vertices. Since reversal has no invariant nonempty face it acts fixed-point-freely geometrically; the Lefschetz trace on the sphere gives (-1)^m (m=1 treated separately). Independent complete arc-mask checks for six small branched/disconnected forests tested 2,450 faces and 2,240 domination incidences.

final_claim: For any finite forest F with m>=1 edges, once subdivide each edge and bidirect every new edge. The multipath complex of directed vertex-simple paths simplicially collapses onto the m-fold join of S^0, hence S^(m-1) integrally, and global arrow reversal acts by (-1)^m on its unique reduced homology generator.
